dast_data.verbose_404: The 404 error page reveals its technology or an error trace ({framework})
finding.dast_data.verbose_404: The error page of a non-existent URL reveals technical information ({frameworks}).
module.dast_data.checks: Finds headers that announce a software version or a debug mode, and inspects the error page of a non-existent URL (stack traces, file paths, a framework's debug page).
module.dast_data.fix:
Turn debug mode off in production immediately and remove the debug headers (`X-Debug-Token`, `X-Debug-Token-Link`, `X-Debug`, `X-WT-TTL`, `X-WT-TS`): Symfony `APP_ENV=prod` and `APP_DEBUG=0`, Laravel `APP_ENV=production` and `APP_DEBUG=false`, Django `DEBUG = False`, Flask or Werkzeug (never run `app.run(debug=True)` in production, go through gunicorn or uWSGI), PHP `display_errors = Off`.
Other stacks: Spring Boot `server.error.include-stacktrace=never`; ASP.NET, debugging disabled and `customErrors` enabled in `web.config`; Node.js and Express `NODE_ENV=production`; Rails `RAILS_ENV=production`.
If a debug console or profiler was reachable (Werkzeug Debugger, Symfony Profiler, Laravel Whoops page, Django debug page), treat the application secrets as exposed: renew the application key (`APP_KEY`, `SECRET_KEY`), the database passwords and the API tokens that appeared in the configuration or in the traces.
Replace the 404 and 500 error pages with plain pages, with no stack trace, no file path and no framework or server version, and record the details in the server logs only.
Hide the versions announced in headers (`Server`, `X-Powered-By`, `X-AspNet-Version`, `X-AspNetMvc-Version`, `X-Generator`): nginx `server_tokens off`, Apache `ServerTokens Prod` and `ServerSignature Off`, PHP `expose_php = Off`, IIS and ASP.NET (see the snippet), Express `app.disable("x-powered-by")`. A header without a version number (`Server: nginx`) is acceptable.
If the headers come from a server behind a reverse proxy, remove them on the proxy too (`proxy_hide_header X-Powered-By;` with nginx, `Header always unset X-Powered-By` with Apache).
Update the announced software: hiding the version does not fix known flaws, it only avoids pointing at them.
Check: `curl -sI https://example.com | grep -iE '^(server|x-powered-by|x-aspnet|x-generator|x-debug)'` must no longer show a version or a debug header, and `curl -si https://example.com/page-that-does-not-exist` must show a plain 404 page. Then run the scan again.
module.dast_data.fix_snippet:
# nginx
server_tokens off;
proxy_hide_header X-Powered-By;
proxy_hide_header X-Debug-Token;
proxy_hide_header X-Debug-Token-Link;
fastcgi_hide_header X-Powered-By;

# Apache
ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
Header always unset X-Powered-By

# php.ini
expose_php = Off
display_errors = Off
log_errors = On

# IIS
<configuration>
  <system.web>
    <httpRuntime enableVersionHeader="false" />
    <customErrors mode="On" />
  </system.web>
  <system.webServer>
    <security>
      <requestFiltering removeServerHeader="true" />
    </security>
    <httpProtocol>
      <customHeaders>
        <remove name="X-Powered-By" />
      </customHeaders>
    </httpProtocol>
  </system.webServer>
</configuration>
module.dast_data.title: Disclosures (versions, debug, 404)
module.dast_data.why: A precise version or an error trace helps an attacker pick the right flaw. A debug mode left on in production can expose code or secrets.
